issues.legal_issue: A prayer for injunction based on a disputed title is consequential, and when the declaratory claim is time-barred, the dependent injunction claim is also time-barred.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought cancellation of a registered sale deed and a declaration that it was not binding, along with an injunction concerning the land.

The registered sale deed stated that the purchaser had received possession, and the purchaser’s name was recorded as owner and cultivator from the year after the sale until the suit was filed approximately 22 years later.

The plaintiff claimed possession and cultivation of part of the land, but the court held that she would have had knowledge of the registered deed and the continuing revenue entries through due diligence.
The declaratory and cancellation claims were rejected, and that rejection became final; the injunction was sought to protect possession in the context of those claims.
issues.conclusion: The injunction was consequential to the declaratory and cancellation claims, so the limitation bar applying to those substantive claims also barred the injunction claim.
issues.legal_principle: Under Dilboo v. Dhanraji (2000) 7 SCC 702, registration gives deemed knowledge of a document, and a plaintiff disputing limitation must aver and prove that the claim is within time; knowledge may also be attributed where due diligence would have disclosed the relevant facts. Although an injunction is ordinarily a substantive relief whose limitation period may run from interference with possession, that approach does not apply where the injunction is consequential to a declaration that is itself time-barred.

rule.if: suit_seeks_declaration_and_dependent_injunction and title_document_was_registered and public_records_consistently_showed_another_person_as_owner_or_cultivator and claimant_asserted_possession_or_cultivation and declaratory_claim_is_time_barred

predicates.suit_seeks_declaration_and_dependent_inj: The claimant brought a suit seeking a declaration about title together with an injunction that depends on that title claim.
predicates.title_document_was_registered: A document recording the competing title was registered.
predicates.public_records_consistently_showed_anoth: Public land records continuously identified another person as owner or cultivator of the land.
predicates.claimant_asserted_possession_or_cultivat: The claimant asserted possession of, or cultivation on, the land, making the recorded entries discoverable through due diligence.
predicates.declaratory_claim_is_time_barred: The claim for a declaration concerning title is outside the applicable limitation period.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks an injunction dependent on a declaration of title, and the recorded title information was discoverable through due diligence but the declaratory claim is time-barred, the dependent injunction claim is also time-barred.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant whose title has been decided against them cannot obtain an injunction against the person established to be the true owner merely by asserting possession.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought cancellation of the registered sale deed and a declaration concerning title, but those claims were rejected and the rejection became final.
The sale deed in favour of the defendant was accepted as valid, including its recording of full consideration, and the defendant was held to be the true and absolute owner.
The lower courts found the plaintiff in possession of part of the land, but the Supreme Court considered the claim even on the assumption that she was in possession.
The plaintiff sought an injunction to prevent the true owner from disturbing that possession.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was not entitled to a permanent injunction against the true owner; the injunction decree was unsustainable and was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: A bare injunction suit may be maintainable in appropriate circumstances, but a claimant cannot maintain one against the true owner after the title dispute has been settled against the claimant. Under Jharkhand State Housing Board v. Didar Singh (2019) 17 SCC 692, a genuine cloud over title may require a declaration; here title was settled against the claimant. A person in possession may have a good title against the world except the rightful owner, as stated in A. Subramanian v. R. Pannerselvam (2021) 3 SCC 675, but cannot use that possession to obtain an injunction against the rightful owner. Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (2008) 4 SCC 594 concerns lawful possession; possession after the claimant has failed to establish title against the true owner is not lawful possession entitling the claimant to an injunction.

predicates.suit_seeks_injunction_against_alleged_tr: The claimant sought an injunction preventing another person alleged to own the property from disturbing the claimant’s possession.
predicates.title_dispute_was_adjudicated_against_cl: A competent court resolved the title dispute against the claimant.
predicates.opposing_owner_was_established_as_true_o: The opposing person was established to hold the rightful title to the property.
predicates.claimant_lacked_independent_legal_entitl: The claimant had no legal entitlement to remain in possession independent of the title claim decided against them.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks an injunction against the established true owner after losing the title dispute and has no independent legal entitlement to possession, the claimant cannot obtain that injunction.

issues.legal_issue: A competent court’s adjudication of the rights of a person in possession and the true owner satisfies due process, so the owner need not bring a further suit before relying on that adjudication.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought a protective injunction against the defendant, who was held to be the true owner under a registered sale deed.
The plaintiff’s title claims were adjudicated and rejected, and the injunction claim was considered and ultimately dismissed by the courts.
The plaintiff argued that even if the defendant was the true owner, the defendant had to bring a separate suit to recover possession.
issues.conclusion: The prior adjudication satisfied due process; the defendant was not required to bring a separate suit before the injunction claim could be dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Maria Margarida Sequeira Fernandes v. Erasmo Jack de Sequeira (2012) 5 SCC 370 explains that due process protects a person in settled possession from forcible dispossession, but is satisfied when a competent court adjudicates the parties’ rights. It approved Thomas Cook (India) Ltd. v. Hotel Imperial (2006) 88 DRJ 545, which explains that it does not matter which party initiated the proceeding: adjudication of the protective claim satisfies the requirement of recourse to law.

predicates.person_in_possession_sought_protective_i: A person in possession asked a court to prevent another person from dispossessing them.
predicates.competent_court_adjudicated_the_parties_: A court with jurisdiction considered and determined the parties’ rights concerning the property.
predicates.claimant_failed_to_establish_entitlement: The person seeking protection failed to establish a legal basis for the requested injunction.

issues.definition: When a person in possession seeks protective relief and a competent court adjudicates the parties’ rights but denies that relief, the adjudication satisfies due process without requiring the owner to bring a further suit.
